findings.title: Ec2 Imdsv1 Optional
findings.description: The current configuration has http_tokens set to 'optional', which allows IMDSv1 and makes the instance vulnerable to SSRF attacks. By changing it to 'required', we ensure that only IMDSv2 is used, which is more secure. This change enforces the use of IMDSv2 and mitigates the vulnerability.
findings.fix_hint: Update the http_tokens value to 'required' to enforce IMDSv2 and prevent SSRF attacks

findings.title: Xentinel Hardcoded Aws Access Key
findings.description: Hardcoding sensitive credentials like AWS access keys and database passwords poses a significant security risk, as they can be exposed to unauthorized parties. Using environment variables to store these credentials helps to keep them secure and separate from the codebase. This approach also makes it easier to manage and rotate credentials without modifying the code.
findings.fix_hint: Use environment variables to store sensitive credentials
findings.fixed_code:
import os
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = os.environ.get('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID')
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = os.environ.get('AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY')
DB_PASSWORD = os.environ.get('DB_PASSWORD')
STRIPE_SECRET = os.environ.get('STRIPE_SECRET')

findings.title: Xentinel Hardcoded Aws Secret
findings.description: Hardcoding AWS secret access keys poses a significant security risk as it can lead to immediate account takeover. Using environment variables to store sensitive credentials is a more secure approach as it keeps them separate from the codebase. This way, even if the code is exposed, the credentials remain protected.
findings.fix_hint: Use environment variables to store sensitive credentials

findings.title: Tainted Sql String
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly inserts user input into the SQL query. By using a parameterized query, the input is treated as a literal value, preventing an attacker from injecting malicious SQL. This fix ensures that the query is executed safely, regardless of the user input.
findings.cwe: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
findings.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection attacks
findings.fixed_code: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?"; result = conn.execute(query, (user_id,)).fetchall()

findings.title: Subprocess Injection
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to command injection because it uses shell=True and passes user input directly to the subprocess call. By passing arguments as a list, we avoid the need for shell=True and prevent an attacker from injecting malicious commands. This fix ensures that only the ping command with the specified arguments can be executed.
findings.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Use the subprocess module with a dictionary to allowlist a set of commands and avoid shell injection by passing arguments as a list instead of a string with shell=True

findings.title: Dangerous Subprocess Use
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to command injection because it directly uses user-controlled input in the subprocess function. Using shlex.quote() ensures that the input is properly escaped, preventing malicious actors from injecting arbitrary commands. This fix assumes that the shlex library is imported with 'import shlex'
findings.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Use the shlex library to escape user-controlled input for the subprocess function

findings.title: Subprocess Shell True
findings.description: The original code uses shell=True, which can lead to command injection attacks. By passing the command and arguments as a list, we avoid invoking a shell and reduce the risk of injection. This change ensures that only the intended ping command is executed, without allowing arbitrary shell commands.
findings.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Replace the subprocess call with a safer alternative that avoids shell injection

findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The vulnerability is caused by directly using user-provided input in the filename, allowing an attacker to traverse the file system. To fix this, we need to validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks. The provided fixed code checks for invalid filenames and prevents traversal attacks by checking for "/../" in the filename.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks

findings.title: Xentinel Sql Injection Format
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly interpolates user input into the query string. Using parameterized queries with the '?' placeholder and passing the user input as an array to the query method prevents the input from being executed as SQL code. This fix ensures that the input is treated as literal input, not as part of the SQL command.
findings.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
findings.fixed_code: const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?'; conn.query(query, [username, password], (err, results) => { callback(results && results.length > 0); });

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted RDP (port 3389)
findings.description: The current security group rule allows unrestricted access to RDP on port 3389, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to restrict the access to only trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group rule to include a specific CIDR block, we can prevent unauthorized access to the RDP port.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group rule to only allow RDP access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks
findings.fixed_code: aws_security_group_rule.app_sg_rule { type = "ingress" from_port = 3389 to_port = 3389 protocol = "tcp" cidr_blocks = ["192.168.1.0/24"] }

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The current security group rule allows unrestricted SSH access on port 22, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to restrict the access to a specific IP address or range. By updating the security group rule to only allow access from a trusted IP range, we can prevent unauthorized access to the instance.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group rule to only allow SSH access from a specific IP address or range
findings.fixed_code: aws_security_group_rule.app_sg_rule { type = "ingress" from_port = 22 to_port = 22 protocol = "tcp" cidr_blocks = ["192.168.1.0/24"] }

findings.title: RDS instance publicly accessible
findings.description: The RDS instance is currently publicly accessible, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, the 'publicly_accessible' attribute should be set to 'false' to restrict access to the instance. This change will prevent unauthorized access to the database instance.
findings.fix_hint: Set the 'publicly_accessible' attribute to 'false' for the 'aws_db_instance' resource

findings.title: S3 bucket allows public ACL
findings.description: The current configuration allows public access to the S3 bucket, which is a critical security risk. By setting the ACL to private, only authorized users can access the bucket. This change should be applied to the aws_s3_bucket resource in the main.tf file.
findings.fix_hint: Set the ACL of the S3 bucket to private to prevent public access

findings.title: S3 bucket allows public ACL
findings.description: TERRAFORM check CKV_AWS_20 failed on resource 'AWS::S3::Bucket.AppBucket'.
findings.fix_hint: Set the ACL of the S3 bucket to private to prevent public access

findings.title: S3 Block Public Access not enabled
findings.description: The S3 Block Public Access feature prevents public access to S3 buckets, which is a critical security control. By enabling this feature, you can prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data stored in the AppBucket. This can be achieved by adding the block_public_access configuration to the AppBucket resource in the Terraform configuration.
findings.fix_hint: Enable S3 Block Public Access on the AppBucket resource

findings.title: S3 bucket allows public policy
findings.description: The current S3 bucket policy allows public access, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to update the policy to deny all public access. This can be achieved by adding a bucket policy that explicitly denies any actions on the bucket and its objects to all principals.
findings.fix_hint: Update the S3 bucket policy to restrict public access

findings.title: IAM policy allows wildcard resource (*)
findings.description: The current IAM policy allows access to all resources in the account due to the wildcard (*) in the Resource field. This is a critical security risk as it grants excessive permissions. By specifying explicit resources, such as the ARN of a specific S3 bucket, access can be restricted to only the necessary resources.
findings.fix_hint: Update the IAM policy to specify explicit resources instead of using a wildcard (*)

findings.title: Admin Managed Policy: AdministratorAccess
findings.description: The current policy grants unrestricted AWS access, violating the principle of least privilege. A custom policy or the AmazonLambdaExecute managed policy should be used instead, which only grants necessary permissions for the Lambda function to execute. This change will help prevent potential security risks associated with over-privileged roles.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the AdministratorAccess policy with a custom policy that only grants necessary permissions for the AppLambdaRole

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: iam:*
findings.description: The current policy grants full IAM control, which is a critical security risk. By replacing 'iam:*' with specific required actions like 'iam:PassRole', 'iam:GetRole', and 'iam:ListRoles', we limit the policy to only necessary permissions. This change prevents potential privilege escalation and reduces the attack surface.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the 'iam:*' action with specific required actions in the AppInlinePolicy

findings.title: Privilege Escalation Path Detected
findings.description: The original policy allows the DeployUser to create a Lambda function with any role, which is a privilege escalation path. The fixed policy restricts the DeployUser to only create Lambda functions and pass the app-lambda-role, preventing arbitrary code execution as admin. This change ensures that the DeployUser can only perform necessary actions and cannot escalate privileges.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the AppInlinePolicy to only allow necessary actions and resources

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: *
findings.description: The current policy grants all AWS permissions to the lambda function, which is a security risk. To fix this, we need to specify the exact actions required by the lambda function, such as logging actions. By replacing the wildcard action with a specific set of actions, we can reduce the attack surface and follow the principle of least privilege.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the wildcard action with a specific set of actions required by the lambda function

findings.title: Admin Policy Reference: AdministratorAccess
findings.description: The AdministratorAccess policy grants full AWS access, which is a security risk. A custom policy should be created to grant only the necessary permissions, such as logging access, to the lambda execution role. This fix replaces the AdministratorAccess policy with a custom policy that grants only the required permissions.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the AdministratorAccess policy with a custom policy that grants only the necessary permissions for the lambda execution role

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The RDS instance is missing logging, which can cause important event information to be lost. Enabling logging through CloudWatch will provide visibility into database events. The 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' argument can be used to specify the types of logs to export, such as error, general, and slowquery logs.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the RDS instance by setting the 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' argument

findings.title: Rds Insecure Password Storage In Source Code
findings.description: The hardcoded password in the aws_db_instance resource is a security risk, as it can be accessed by anyone with access to the Terraform configuration files. To fix this, a random password can be generated using the random_password resource and used in the aws_db_instance resource. This ensures that the password is not stored in plain text and is unique for each deployment.
findings.fix_hint: Use the aws_db_instance resource with a random password generated by the random_password resource
findings.fixed_code:
resource "aws_db_instance" "app_db" {
  identifier             = "app-database"
  engine                 = "mysql"
  engine_version         = "8.0"
  instance_class         = "db.t3.micro"
  allocated_storage      = 20
  db_name                = "appdb"
  username               = "admin"
  password               = random_password.app_db_password.result
  publicly_accessible    = true
  skip_final_snapshot    = true
  storage_encrypted      = false
  deletion_protection    = false
}

resource "random_password" "app_db_password" {
  length = 16
  special = true
}

findings.title: Aws Ec2 Has Public Ip
findings.description: The EC2 instance has a public IP address attached, which poses a security risk by allowing public access to the instance. To fix this, the associate_public_ip_address attribute should be set to false, ensuring that the instance is not accessible from the internet. This change will help prevent unauthorized access to the instance.
findings.cwe: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
findings.fix_hint: Set associate_public_ip_address to false to prevent public IP address attachment

findings.title: Sql Injection Db Cursor Execute
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly formats user input into the query string, allowing an attacker to inject malicious SQL code. By using a parameterized query, the execute method will treat the user input as a literal value instead of part of the SQL code, preventing the injection. This fix assumes that the sqlite3 library is being used, which supports parameterized queries with the '?' placeholder.
findings.cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection by passing user input as a parameter to the execute method instead of directly formatting it into the query string

findings.title: Avoid_App_Run_With_Bad_Host
findings.description: Running the Flask app with host 0.0.0.0 makes it accessible from any IP address, which is a security risk. Changing the host to 127.0.0.1 restricts access to the local machine. Additionally, debug mode should be set to False in production to prevent exposure of full stack traces.
findings.cwe: CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
findings.fix_hint: Change the host parameter in the app.run function to a specific IP address or localhost to prevent public exposure

findings.title: Debug Enabled
findings.description: The debug mode in Flask should be disabled in production to prevent sensitive information leakage. Setting debug to False will prevent full stack traces from being exposed. Environment variables can also be used to configure the debug mode for more flexibility.
findings.fix_hint: Set the debug mode to False or configure it using environment variables

findings.title: Direct Response Write
findings.description: The current implementation directly writes user input to the response, making it vulnerable to XSS attacks. To fix this, use a template engine like EJS or Pug to render HTML and automatically escape user input. This ensures that any user-provided data is properly sanitized and cannot be used for malicious purposes.
findings.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.fix_hint: Use template engine to render HTML and escape user input

findings.title: Raw Html Format
findings.description: The current implementation directly interpolates user input into HTML, making it vulnerable to XSS attacks. Sanitizing the input using DOMPurify prevents malicious code from being executed. This fix assumes that the DOMPurify library is installed and imported in the code.
findings.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.fix_hint: Use a templating engine or a library like DOMPurify to sanitize user input before rendering it in HTML

findings.title: Security group unrestricted ingress

attack_chains.title: Cloud Infrastructure Takeover
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains access to the cloud infrastructure by exploiting hardcoded AWS credentials in the code, then uses the unrestricted security group rules to access the RDS instance and exfiltrate sensitive data.
steps: Step 1: attacker reads hardcoded AWS access key and secret using finding 5f54ec0a in file xentinel-demo-repo/src/app.py
Step 2: this gives them access to the cloud infrastructure, which they use to exploit finding 5d7aa323 in file uploaded_repo/xentinel-demo-repo/infra/main.tf to access the RDS instance
attack_chains.remediation: Remove hardcoded AWS credentials from the code

attack_chains.title: Privilege Escalation and Data Exfiltration
attack_chains.description: An attacker escalates their privileges by exploiting a privilege escalation path in the IAM policy, then uses the elevated privileges to exfiltrate sensitive data from the S3 bucket.
steps: Step 1: attacker exploits privilege escalation path using finding 8655ceaf in file xentinel-demo-repo/infra/stack.json
Step 2: this gives them elevated privileges, which they use to exploit finding 66cb4590 in file uploaded_repo/xentinel-demo-repo/infra/main.tf to access the S3 bucket
attack_chains.remediation: Remove the privilege escalation path from the IAM policy

attack_chains.title: Code Execution and Data Exfiltration
attack_chains.description: An attacker executes arbitrary code on the server by exploiting a subprocess injection vulnerability in the code, then uses the executed code to exfiltrate sensitive data from the database.
steps: Step 1: attacker exploits subprocess injection using finding caae0435 in file xentinel-demo-repo/src/app.py
Step 2: this gives them code execution capabilities, which they use to exploit finding 8d176e82 in file xentinel-demo-repo/src/auth.js to extract sensitive data from the database
attack_chains.remediation: Remove the subprocess injection vulnerability from the code
